assets.publisher: Ministry of Environment, Province of British Columbia

assets.dateNote: The cover is undated. “BC Environment” beside the flag symbol places it in the flag years; the Ministry of Environment of 1988–1991, between Environment and Parks and Environment, Lands and Parks, is the ministry of that name, which is where it is placed. Whether the name and mark carried on under Environment, Lands and Parks from 1991 is not established.
assets.notes: “BC” in bold sans serif beside the flag symbol, with “Environment” below, tightly set. Printed in cream on a green band running diagonally across a cover photograph; drawn here upright in one dark ink.

assets.fidelityNote: A supplied vector reconstruction (revision 2), not original artwork. The flag is the gallery’s own twelve-path flag (src/assets/flagMark.js), every path unchanged and placed as one unit; the stars are regular five-point shapes (inner radius 0.445) placed on the reference’s landmarks, where the dense base of the spray, merged in print, is partly inferred; “SUPERHOST” is drawn from eight custom serif letter masters and “Expect the most” from ten brush-stroke skeletons swept with a mathematical nib, both refitted to the references in the second revision. The original typefaces are not identified. Overlap of the lettering with the references (intersection over union at a 0.5 threshold): wordmark 0.70 and script 0.58 against the newspaper, 0.83 and 0.64 against the trademark specimen. The two references set the stars differently, so each layout is reconstructed on its own rather than one being stretched to the other.

assets.label: Thompson Health Region: symbol, name and tagline, vector reconstruction
assets.sourceLocator: Rebuilt from the region’s letterheads of 9 September 1999, 9 June 2000 and 1 November 2001, in the City of Merritt’s council agendas (PDF pages 118, 110 and 53); the symbol’s colours from a 2003 Environment Canada publication
assets.dateNote: The letters date sightings of the logo from 1999 to 2001, not its adoption.
assets.notes: A cross split by a winding white path, five pointed cut-outs across its top, beside “Thompson Health Region” in serif and “A Path to Better Health” in italic, in black as on the region’s letterheads.
assets.fidelityNote: A vector reconstruction, not original artwork, which has not been found. The symbol (a cross with a winding white path and five pointed cut-outs at the top) is redrawn as smooth curves over three letterheads of 1999–2001; their scans carry about 112 px of real detail, so its exact curves and corner radii are not recoverable, and the damaged upper-left edge of the 1999 copy is restored from the later two. The name is outlined EB Garamond (weight 500) and the tagline Nimbus Roman Italic, fitted to the letterheads’ ink; the original typefaces are not identified, and these set a little heavier than the letters’ thin print.
